Chapter 01 of 18

The Morning Meeting

AssembleTrout Lake80 BPM
The story

Every morning, before the sun comes up, representatives of Terminal City gather at Trout Lake to decide what kind of day it is going to be. The crows arrive first, because crows are always first. The coyotes stay back at the edge of the park, pretending they are not interested. A faint static gathers in the reeds, like a radio caught between stations. And the water listens.

Nobody has ever figured out who runs the meeting. There is no chairperson, no agenda and no minutes. What the meeting decides is not written down anywhere. It simply happens, the way weather happens, and then it is over. By the time the first joggers and dog-walkers reach the lake, the representatives have gone and the park looks like an ordinary park.

There is one way to tell whether the meeting is in session. Look at the water. If Trout Lake is perfectly still, not a ripple, not a ring, then the meeting is happening right now. Hold still. Gather here. Before the city wakes, it has to start again.

Field notes
The ruleIf Trout Lake is perfectly still, the meeting is in session.
HOLD STILLGATHER HEREBEFORE THE CITYSTART AGAIN

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
